- **Two-nexiom machine:** {ruvidi, funozes}, {nukape, ruvidi}, {nukape, funozes}, {bokiril, ruvidi} or {bokiril, funozes}.

Two tests can separate at most 4 outcomes, so I'll split these 8 into two groups of 4. Next I'll test nukape, ruvidi and vabunan:
- **If it lights up (4 left):** it is one of the three one-nexiom pairs, or a two-nexiom machine with {nukape, ruvidi}.
- **If it stays dark (4 left):** it is a two-nexiom machine with {ruvidi, funozes}, {nukape, funozes}, {bokiril, ruvidi} or {bokiril, funozes}.

One test can only split these into two groups, so the best I can do is 2 and 2. I'll then have to choose between two equally likely answers. Next I'll test ruvidi alone:
- **If it lights up:** it is a one-nexiom machine with {ruvidi, funozes} or {ruvidi, vabunan}.
- **If it stays dark:** it is a one-nexiom machine with {funozes, vabunan}, or a two-nexiom machine with {nukape, ruvidi}.

Three yes/no tests give at most 8 outcomes, so I can't be sure of a perfect answer. I'll keep splitting the possibilities as evenly as I can.

Next I'll test logarar (from the first group) with venekis (from the other group):
- **Lights up (7 cases):** only possible under "needs one." The pair includes logarar or venekis: logarar–tusafes, logarar–bonovun, logarar–venekis, logarar–lilusir, logarar–vibigek, tusafes–venekis, bonovun–venekis.
- **Stays dark (8 cases):** under "needs one," the pair avoids both, leaving tusafes–bonovun, tusafes–lilusir, tusafes–vibigek, bonovun–lilusir and bonovun–vibigek. Under "needs two," any of the 3 pairs within logarar, tusafes and bonovun also stays dark.

Four possibilities remain under "needs one": tusafes–bonovun, tusafes–lilusir, tusafes–vibigek, bonovun–lilusir and bonovun–vibigek. Three remain under "needs two": logarar–tusafes, logarar–bonovun and tusafes–bonovun. That is 8 cases.

Two tests give at most 4 outcomes, so I can't be sure of a perfect answer. Testing tusafes with lilusir splits the cases 4/4:
- **Lights up (4 cases):** only possible under "needs one." The pair is tusafes–bonovun, tusafes–lilusir, tusafes–vibigek or bonovun–lilusir.
- **Stays dark (4 cases):** either "needs one" with bonovun–vibigek, or "needs two" with logarar–tusafes, logarar–bonovun or tusafes–bonovun.

TEST: tusafes, lilusir

- tusafes–lilusir
- tusafes–vibigek
- bonovun–lilusir

- **Lights up:** the pair is tusafes–lilusir or bonovun–lilusir.
- **Stays dark:** the pair is tusafes–bonovun or tusafes–vibigek.

After this test I will have to guess between the last two pairs.

Result: the machine LIT UP. You have used all your tests. Give your ANSWER now.

The rule is **needs one**. Test 3 (tusafes and lilusir) lit up, and under "needs two" that pair was impossible.

Test 4 (lilusir alone) lit up, so **lilusir is a nexiom**. The other nexiom is either tusafes or bonovun, and my tests can't tell which. Both pairs fit every result:
- **Test 1** lit up because either partner is in the first group.

- **Tests 3 and 4** lit up because of lilusir.

So this answer is a 50/50 guess between those two pairs, and I'm choosing tusafes.
